October 1st, 1936.
Guests. Mr. S. Ohyama (taking place
instead of Mr. K. Katoh).
Mr. Y. Endo, Architect.
Our President Mr. Ehara informed us that
rotarian Sahara is transferred to Mukden,
and is leaving us in the near future. During
these last two years he has been a constant
worker on behalf of the railway. It is not
for us now to sing praises for all his deeds.
As a member of our club has was most
regular in attendance and a true member.
We are sorry to lose him, however we have
to be consoled by the thought that there is
a Rotary Club in Mukden and we are sure
he will join it.
Rotarian B. Katoh is also shortly leaving
us for Bombey. He also had been with us
for more than two years. There in Bombey
we are not sure that he can find a Rotary
Club but if not we sincerly hope that he
will start one.
"I propose to raise our glasses and wish

us with the 7th anniversary of the Club.
Rotarians with their wives were in great
number.

made a speech thanking our guests for

the foundation of the Club here. He also
informed us that this year the number of

that the work of Harbin Rotary Club will

bers would do some good work. With that

of Rotary Clubs. Where last year we had
4000 Rotary Clubs this year we already
have 4200. All the countries have Rotary
Clubs in them and the only sad exception
is the Soviet Russia.
The Ideas of the Rotary Club are very
simple. Rotary gives the possibility of
mutual understanding. It developes a strong
will. It makes people understand different
professions.
People are strongly connected with each
other. Rotarians of One Club are frequently
seen in the Rotary Clubs of different cities.
They visit conferenses. Last time it was
America, next time it will be in Nice.
The chief idea of the Rotary Club is
Service. The idea of self improvement.
International work, and mutual understan-
ding. These are the ideas of Rotary and
we try to bring them to life the best we
can.

by many others.

Gundsi and Kawasumi.

There was a nice Japanese and Russian
programm and everyone went home thin-
king that the time went too quickly.

Constitution of Rotary International
ARTICLE VII
IMPORTANT
READ CAREFULLY
Section 3-Representation. Each member club shall be entitled in any convention of Rotary
International to one (1) delegate for each fifty (50) of its members or major fraction
thereof, honorary members excepted, based upon the membership of the club on the 30th
day of April preceding the convention. Each club shall be entitled to at least one delegate.
Section 4-Attendance. It shall be the duty of each member club to be represented at each
convention of Rotary International by duly accredited delegate or delegates.
Section 5-Votes. Each accredited delegate shall be entitled to cast one vote on each question
submitted to vote in the convention.
The substance of it all is that each club is expected to select a certain one (or certain ones)
of its members as its delegate (or delegates) whether he (or they) can attend or not, and
if he (or they) cannot attend the convention, then designate someone else as the proxy for
each one of the delegates so selected.
By-Laws of Rotary International
ARTICLE VI
Section 4 (c)--Proxies. Any member club located in a country other than that in which the
convention is held may designate as the proxy for any absent delegate or delegates from
such club any active or past service member of its own club, or if unrepresented in the
convention by a delegate or alternate from its own membership such club may designate
as the proxy therefor any active or past service member of any other Rotary club,
wherever located.
Upon delivery of the certificate as provided in Section 5-Credentials of Article VI of
these by-laws, such proxy in addition to any other right to vote that he may have shall
have the right to vote in place of the non-attending delegate or delegates whom
he represents.
Section 5-Credentials. The authority of each delegate and alternate shall be evidenced by a
certificate signed by the president and secretary of his club The authority of a proxy shall
be evidenced by a certificate signed by the president and secretary of the club or clubs for
whose non-attending delegate or delegates he is proxy. All certificates must be delivered
to the Credentials Committee at the convention to entitle delegates, alternates, and proxies,
to participate as such in the convention.
Section 7-Registration Fee. Each Person, sixteen years of age or over, attending a convention
of Rotary International shall register and pay a registration fee of Five Dollars ($5.00)
U. S. Currency. No elector shall be entitled to vote in the convention unless and until
his registration fee has been paid.

Constitution of Rotary International
ARTICLE VII
IMPORTANT
READ CAREFULLY
Section 3-Representation. Each member club shall be entitled in any convention of Rotary
International to one (1) delegate for each fifty (50) of its members or major fraction
thereof, honorary members excepted, based upon the membership of the club on the
30th day of April preceding the convention. Each club shall be entitled to at least one
delegate.
Section 4-Attendance. It shall be the duty of each member club to be represented at each
convention of Rotary International by duly accredited delegate or delegates.
Section 5-Votes. Each accredited delegate shall be entitled to cast one vote on each
question submitted to vote in the convention.
The substance of it all is that each club is expected to select a certain one (or certain
ones) of its members as its delegate (or delegates) whether he (or they) can attend or
not, and if he (or they) cannot attend the convention, then designate someone else as
the proxy for each one of the delegates so selected.
By-Laws of Rotary International
ARTICLE VI
Section 4 (c)-Proxies. Any member club may designate as the proxy for any absent dele-
gate or delegates of the club any active or past service member of its own club, or, if
unrepresented in the convention by one of its own members, any active or past service
member of any other Rotary club within its own district, provided that a club which is
not located within a district may designate as the proxy for its non-attending delegate
or delegates any active or past service member of any Rotary club, wherever located.
Upon delivery of the certificate as provided in Section 5-Credentials of Article VI of
these by-laws, such proxy in addition to any other right to vote that he may have shall
have the right to vote in place of the non-attending delegate or delegates whom he
represents.
Section 5-Credentials. The authority of each delegate and alternate shall be evidenced by
a certificate signed by the president and secretary of his club. The authority of a proxy
shall be evidenced by a certificate signed by the president and secretary of the club
or clubs for whose non-attending delegate or delegates he is proxy. All certificates
must be delivered to the Credentials Committee at the convention to entitle delegates,
alternates, and proxies, to participate as such in the convention.
Section 7-Registration Fee. Each Person, sixteen years of age or over, attending a conven-
tion of Rotary International shall register and pay a registration fee of Five Dollars
(5.00) United States Currency. No elector shall be entitled to vote in the convention
unless and until his registration fee has been paid.
